chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman with a thousand dirhams, so he gave her an absconded slave of his and a silken gown, as the thousand dirhams which was her dower. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she was pleased with the slave and had known it, so there is no problem when she takes possession of the cloth and is pleased with the slave.' I said, 'Supposing he divorces her before he enters with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no dower for her, and she returns to him five hundred dirhams, and the slave becomes hers.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He entered with her (consummated the marriage)
key_terms.عَبْدًا: Slave (male or female, contextually female here)
key_terms.مَهْر: Dower or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dower if a man divorces his wife before consummation when the dower includes a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the nature of dower (mahr) as a contractual gift rather than a fixed monetary debt, illustrating that if the wife accepts a specific asset like an absconded slave, she retains ownership of that asset even in the event of pre-consummation divorce. Scholarly context highlights the Shia emphasis on mutual consent and the actual possession (qabd) of the dower items, distinguishing this from the Hanafi view where half the dower is typically due regardless of possession. The ruling underscores the principle that the dower is a right of the wife that can be satisfied by specific goods agreed upon at the time of marriage.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Al Fuzayl who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who married a woman with a thousand Dirhams (as dower), so he gave her an absconded slave of his and a silken gown with a thousand Dirhams which was her dower. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she was pleased with the slave and had known it, so there is no problem when she takes possession of the cloth, and is pleased with the slave’. 
I said, ‘Supposing he divorces her before he copulates with her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is dower for her, and she would have to return five hundred Dirhams back to him, and the slave would come to be for her’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from al-Fudayl who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman for one thousand dirham. He then gives her a runaway slave and a gown made of silk for one thousand dirham for her mahr (dower). He (the Imam) said, ‘If she agrees for the slave and knows his condition, then it is not unlawful if she takes possession of the clothes and has agreed for the slave.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if he divorces her before going to bed with her?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘She will have no mahr (dower) and has to return five hundred dirham and the slave is for her.’”
